In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CaC6 is a superconductor whose Tc is reduced by an order-disorder structural phase transition, which takes place at P ≈ 9 GPa.
the CaC6 phase diagram is not a simple one and is characterized by several different phase transitions.

the CaC6 superconductivity is strongly affected by the disorder of the Ca sublattices.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the CaC6 structure is not a good candidate to explain the recently discovered superconductivity at high pressure in graphite intercalated compounds.

, contrary to the case of graphite intercalation compounds where disorder in the carbon layer is the main cause of Tc reduction, in CaC6, the disorder in the intercalated layer, i.e. the Ca sublattices, is the key factor to understand the Tc reduction.
